1	---
2	title: "Subjects in the picture"
3	description: "What Frame Job finds in a clip's picture on this Mac, what it doesn't know about the people in it, and when a file gets analysed."
4	---
5	
6	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
7	
8	Frame Job can find who and what is in a clip's picture: faces, people and the parts the eye goes to first. Its framing tools use this to keep a subject in shot on a canvas of a different shape.
9	
10	<AtAGlance
11	  menu={['Clip ▸ Follow Subject…', 'File ▸ Make Vertical Version…', 'View ▸ Show Subjects']}
12	  tools={['get_media_analysis', 'reframe_clip', 'make_vertical_version']}
13	  needs="Nothing. Apple's Vision framework does this on your Mac, with no key and no upload."
14	/>
15	
16	## What is found
17	
18	Frame Job looks at the picture ten times a second of the file's own time, so a clip you've slowed down or sped up doesn't change what's found. It keeps three things from each look.
19	
20	### Faces
21	
22	Each face's box, how it's turned, and how open the mouth is. Faces in a sample are listed from left to right. See [Faces](/projects/media-analysis/#faces) under media analysis.
23	
24	### People
25	
26	Each person's head and shoulders, as a box. A person's box can stand in for their face while the face can't be found.
27	
28	### Salient regions
29	
30	The parts of the picture the eye goes to first, as boxes. In a talking-head shot this is usually the speaker. On a slide it's often the text. See [People and salient regions](/projects/media-analysis/#people-and-salient-regions) under media analysis.
31	
32	[Show Subjects](/framing/show-subjects/) draws all three over the preview, so you can see what Frame Job has to work with.
33	
34	## Boxes, not people
35	
36	Each sample stands alone. A box has no name, and nothing records that a box in one sample is the same person as a box in the next. Frame Job never puts a name to a face, and it doesn't recognise anyone.
37	
38	[Follow Subject](/framing/follow-subject/#which-subject-it-follows) works out who's who for itself each time it plans, from how the boxes overlap from one sample to the next. That reasoning isn't kept, and it stops at a shot change. Someone who leaves the shot for more than a second and comes back counts as someone new.
39	
40	## When a file is analysed
41	
42	Importing a file doesn't analyse its picture. A file is analysed when something asks for it:
43	
44	- **Clip ▸ Follow Subject…**
45	- **File ▸ Make Vertical Version…**
46	- [**Clip ▸ Switch by Speaker…**](/multicam/one-microphone/), when it cuts from faces
47	- An agent, with `get_media_analysis`, `reframe_clip` or `make_vertical_version`
48	
49	Follow Subject, Make Vertical Version and `reframe_clip` ask only for the part of the file each clip plays, plus a second either side. **View ▸ Show Subjects** never asks, so turning it on costs nothing.
50	
51	Analysis runs in the background and keeps what it has found if it's stopped. Asking again continues from there, and a part that's already been analysed isn't read again. What's found is kept in the project's cache, so a file is only analysed once.
52	
53	[On-device media analysis](/projects/media-analysis/#analysis-happens-on-demand) covers this in full, including [the Analyzing sheet](/projects/media-analysis/#the-analyzing-sheet) and [how background jobs run](/projects/media-analysis/#analysis-runs-in-the-background).
54	
55	## What uses it
56	
57	| Feature | What it uses |
58	| --- | --- |
59	| [Follow Subject](/framing/follow-subject/) | Faces, people and salient regions, to frame the selected clips |
60	| [Make Vertical Version](/framing/make-vertical-version/) | The same, to frame a whole timeline on a tall or square canvas |
61	| [Follow the speaker in a vertical](/framing/follow-speaker/) | Faces and how open each mouth is, to match each microphone to a face |
62	| [Cut from faces with one microphone](/multicam/one-microphone/) | Faces and how open each mouth is, to tell who's talking |
63	| [Show Subjects](/framing/show-subjects/) | All three, drawn over the preview |
64	
65	An agent can frame a clip with the same analysis. See [Reframe a clip (agents)](/framing/reframe-clip/).
66	
67	## Related
68	
69	- [Show Subjects](/framing/show-subjects/)
70	- [Follow Subject](/framing/follow-subject/)
71	- [On-device media analysis](/projects/media-analysis/)
72

1	---
2	title: "Show Subjects"
3	description: "Draw the faces, people and salient regions Frame Job has found for a clip over the preview, so you can see what framing will follow."
4	---
5	
6	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
7	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
8	
9	Show Subjects outlines what Frame Job has found in the selected clip at the playhead, right on the preview. Use it to check what [Follow Subject](/framing/follow-subject/) has to work with.
10	
11	<AtAGlance
12	  menu="View ▸ Show Subjects"
13	  needs="Nothing. It only draws what has already been found."
14	/>
15	
16	## Turn on Show Subjects
17	
18	<Steps>
19	
20	1. Select a clip of a movie.
21	
22	2. Move the playhead to a moment that clip shows.
23	
24	3. Choose **View ▸ Show Subjects**. A tick appears beside it in the menu.
25	
26	</Steps>
27	
28	Select another clip to see its boxes, and move the playhead to see another moment. Choose the item again to turn it off.
29	
30	The item has no shortcut and is always available.
31	
32	It draws for one clip at a time. With several clips selected, that's the front-most one showing at the playhead. A selected still, picture, nest, text, shape or graphic draws nothing and shows no note, and neither does a clip the playhead isn't on.
33	
34	## What the outlines mean
35	
36	| Outline | What it marks |
37	| --- | --- |
38	| Yellow | A face |
39	| Teal | A person's head and shoulders |
40	| Purple, dashed | A salient region, a part of the picture the eye goes to first |
41	
42	Each outline has a dark line behind it, so it stays visible on a bright picture. Faces draw on top of the other two.
43	
44	[Subjects in the picture](/framing/what-is-found/) explains what each kind of box is.
45	
46	## The boxes stay on the picture
47	
48	The boxes sit on the clip's picture wherever you've placed it. If you've moved, scaled or rotated the clip, each box moves and turns with it. If you've cropped the clip, the boxes are clipped to the crop.
49	
50	They also follow the clip's speed, speed ramps and reversal, so they show what the clip is showing at that moment rather than what's at the same time in the file.
51	
52	## Not analyzed
53	
54	When nothing has been found for the clip's picture at the playhead, a note sits at the clip's top-left corner:
55	
56	> Not analyzed — Clip ▸ Follow Subject… analyzes it
57	
58	Show Subjects never starts an analysis, so turning it on costs nothing. To make the boxes, run [Follow Subject](/framing/follow-subject/) or [Make Vertical Version](/framing/make-vertical-version/) on the clip. If Show Subjects is on when an analysis lands, the boxes appear by themselves.
59	
60	Three situations are worth knowing:
61	
62	- Analysis covers the parts of a file that clips play, plus a second either side. Another part of the same file can still read "Not analyzed".
63	- A part that's been analysed and holds nothing shows no outlines and no note.
64	- Follow Subject doesn't analyse a screen recording that has its [cursor file](/recording/cursor-files/), so the note stays on such a clip. See [Screen recordings are skipped](/framing/follow-subject/#screen-recordings-are-skipped).
65	
66	## A view of the window
67	
68	Show Subjects belongs to the window, not the project.
69	
70	- It's off in a new window, and each window has its own setting.
71	- It isn't remembered between launches.
72	- It edits nothing, so it isn't an undo step.
73	- It never changes an export or a saved frame.
74	
75	## With an agent
76	
77	There's no agent tool for the overlay. An agent reads the same boxes with `get_media_analysis`. See [Tools: reading analysis](/mcp/tools-analysis/).
78	
79	## Related
80	
81	- [Subjects in the picture](/framing/what-is-found/)
82	- [Follow Subject](/framing/follow-subject/)
83	- [On-device media analysis](/projects/media-analysis/)
84

1	---
2	title: "Follow Subject"
3	description: "Frame the selected movie clips on the person or thing in them, with eased moves you can edit and a blurred copy behind where the whole picture shows."
4	---
5	
6	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
7	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
8	import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';
9	
10	Follow Subject keeps the person in shot when a clip's picture doesn't fit the canvas, such as a landscape recording on a 1080 × 1920 vertical canvas. It finds the subject, moves the frame with it, and writes each move as an ordinary action you can change.
11	
12	<AtAGlance
13	  menu="Clip ▸ Follow Subject…"
14	  where="Each move, on the clip's action lane"
15	  tools="reframe_clip"
16	  needs="Nothing. Faces, people and shot changes are found on your Mac, with no key and no upload."
17	/>
18	
19	## Frame clips on their subject
20	
21	<Steps>
22	
23	1. Set the canvas you want first, in the [Document tab](/projects/canvas-size/). Follow Subject doesn't change the canvas.
24	
25	2. Select the clips to frame.
26	
27	3. Choose **Clip ▸ Follow Subject…**. It's available when a selected clip plays a movie and no sheet is open, inside a nest too. There's no keyboard shortcut.
28	
29	4. Set [Follow](#follow), [Zoom](#zoom) and [Where Empty](#where-empty).
30	
31	5. Read [the summary](#the-summary) under the controls, which says what will happen.
32	
33	6. Choose **Follow** (<kbd>Return</kbd>), or **Cancel** (<kbd>Esc</kbd>) to leave everything as it was.
34	
35	</Steps>
36	
37	<Shot
38	  name="15i-follow-subject-sheet.sheet"
39	  alt="The Follow Subject sheet, with Follow set to Subject, Zoom at 125 percent and Where Empty set to Show Whole. A summary reads: Finds the faces, people and shot changes in 1 file on this Mac first, then frames 1 clip. Cancel and Follow buttons sit at the bottom right."
40	/>
41	
42	:::tip
43	To change the canvas and frame a whole timeline in one go, use [Make Vertical Version](/framing/make-vertical-version/) instead.
44	:::
45	
46	A still, a picture, a nest, text, a shape, a graphic or an adjustment clip in the selection is left alone, with no line in the summary.
47	
48	## The controls
49	
50	### Follow
51	
52	Follow chooses what the frame stays on.
53	
54	| Choice | What the frame follows |
55	| --- | --- |
56	| **Subject** | A face, or where there's none a person, or where there's neither the region the eye goes to. This is the default. |
57	| **Faces** | Faces only |
58	| **People** | People only |
59	| **Salient Region** | Salient regions only |
60	| **Center** | Nothing. The frame holds on the middle of the picture for the whole clip, with no analysis needed. |
61	
62	### Zoom
63	
64	Zoom sets how tight the frame is, in whole percents from 100 to 400. At 100 % the picture is the smallest it can be and still cover the canvas.
65	
66	It starts at 100 %. If the first selected clip's picture is within 1 % of the canvas's shape, it starts at 125 % instead, because at 100 % such a picture fills the canvas exactly and the frame has no room to move.
67	
68	Zoom enlarges the picture, and so does putting a landscape picture on a tall canvas. A 1080p source on a 1080 × 1920 canvas is already enlarged ×1.78 at 100 %, which can look soft on a phone.
69	
70	### Where Empty
71	
72	Where Empty sets what the frame shows while there's nothing to follow.
73	
74	| Choice | What shows |
75	| --- | --- |
76	| **Show Whole** | The whole picture, with a [blurred copy](#the-blurred-backgrounds-track) filling the canvas around it. This is the default. |
77	| **Center** | The middle of the picture, at the same zoom |
78	
79	It's dimmed while Follow is **Center**.
80	
81	### What's remembered
82	
83	**Follow** and **Where Empty** are remembered for next time, and [Make Vertical Version](/framing/make-vertical-version/) shares them. They're saved when you choose **Follow**, even if you then stop the analysis, and never on **Cancel**. If Make Vertical Version last used **Speaker**, which this sheet doesn't offer, Follow opens on **Subject**. **Zoom** isn't remembered.
84	
85	## The summary
86	
87	Under the controls, the sheet says what **Follow** will do. It updates as you change a control, and after you leave the Zoom field.
88	
89	| The sheet says | What it means |
90	| --- | --- |
91	| "Frames 2 clips." | How many clips will change. |
92	| "Adds a Backgrounds track for the blurred copy." | Some of the framing shows the whole picture, so a [blurred copy](#the-blurred-backgrounds-track) goes behind it. |
93	| "Adds 1 more track behind it where clips overlap." | Two selected clips overlap in time, so their copies need separate tracks. |
94	| "2 actions re-eased at a cut." | A shot change landed inside actions the clip already had, and each was split there and eased again on either side. See [It starts from the whole picture](#it-starts-from-the-whole-picture). |
95	| "1 action carries a framing move." | A move couldn't fit between the clip's own actions, so one of them carries it. |
96	| "Clip 3 is already framed this way." | That clip wouldn't change. |
97	| "Clip 3: …" | That clip can't be framed, and this is why. See [Clips it cannot frame](#clips-it-cannot-frame). |
98	| "Reading the analysis…" | Frame Job is loading what it found earlier. **Follow** is dimmed until it's done. |
99	| "Finds the faces, people and shot changes in 1 file on this Mac first, then frames 1 clip." | The [analysis comes first](#analysis-first). |
100	
101	**Follow** is dimmed when nothing would change.
102	
103	"Clip 3" uses Frame Job's own number for the clip, which isn't its position on the timeline.
104	
105	## Analysis first
106	
107	When the clips haven't been analysed, choosing **Follow** closes the sheet and opens the [Analyzing sheet](/projects/media-analysis/#the-analyzing-sheet) while Frame Job finds what it needs on your Mac. It then frames the clips by itself.
108	
109	The Analyzing sheet has a row for each file and each kind of analysis: **Shot changes**, **Faces**, and **People and salient regions**. Only the part of each file the clip plays is read, plus a second either side.
110	
111	**Stop** changes nothing. **Center** needs no analysis, so it frames at once.
112	
113	Frame Job beeps and frames nothing in these cases, and says why at the foot of the inspector, after **Refused:**
114	
115	| The inspector says | What happened |
116	| --- | --- |
117	| "the project changed while Follow Subject was analyzing, so nothing was framed. Choose Follow Subject again." | The project changed, or you went into or out of a nest, while the analysis ran. What was found is kept, so a second try doesn't start over. |
118	| "The faces analysis of “interview.mov” failed: …" | An analysis couldn't finish. The sentence names the kind and the file. |
119	
120	## It starts from the whole picture
121	
122	Each clip is framed from the whole picture. Its own positions and scales are replaced, both the clip's base values and any an action sets. An action left with nothing to do is removed. The clip's volume and its other actions stay, and so does its crop, which the frame stays inside.
123	
124	The moves then fit around the actions that remain:
125	
126	- A move goes in a gap between them.
127	- A move that would overlap an action starts up to 0.5 s earlier to clear it.
128	- A move that still can't clear is carried by the action it overlaps, along that action's curve.
129	- A shot change that lands inside an action cuts it in three around the one-frame cut. A steady (linear) action plays as it did, and an eased one is eased again on each side.
130	- A speed action, or an action a trim left running past the clip's end, is never cut. It carries the change instead.
131	
132	## How following moves
133	
134	While it follows, the frame stays inside the picture, so nothing past the picture's edge shows.
135	
136	### Which subject it follows
137	
138	When several faces or people are in view, Frame Job scores each on how steadily it's there, how big it is and how central it is, over the second either side and within the shot.
139	
140	It stays with its choice. Another subject takes over only after scoring at least 25 % better for 2 s, so two similar faces don't trade the frame back and forth. With **Subject**, a person's body stands in for their face while the face can't be found.
141	
142	Only the first eight of each kind in a sample count. For faces, that's the eight furthest left.
143	
144	### Where the subject sits
145	
146	| Subject | Where it sits |
147	| --- | --- |
148	| A face | In the middle of the frame, or 38 % of the way down on a frame taller than wide, leaving room below for the rest of the person |
149	| A person | With the top of their box 12 % of the way down the frame |
150	| A salient region | In the middle of the frame |
151	
152	This is where the frame aims. Near the picture's edge it stops at the edge, so the subject sits off from these marks.
153	
154	### Easing and staying put
155	
156	The frame eases onto the subject and moves only when the subject leaves the middle of the frame, so a speaker who sways stays put. The middle counts as 15 % of the frame's width and 12 % of its height either side.
157	
158	A move travels at 0.8 frame widths a second and takes at least 0.4 s. No move starts within 0.5 s of the last one's end, unless the subject has left the frame altogether.
159	
160	### At a shot change
161	
162	The frame cuts with the picture, landing on the first frame of the new shot. It's placed on where the subject sits over the new shot's first second. No move runs across a cut.
163	
164	### When the subject is lost
165	
166	The frame holds for a second, so a blink or a turned head changes nothing. It then follows someone else in the shot if there's anyone. If not, it eases over 0.8 s to your [Where Empty](#where-empty) choice.
167	
168	It comes back once a subject has been in view for 0.6 s.
169	
170	A clip with nobody in view during its first second opens on Where Empty. A clip with nothing to follow at all stays on Where Empty for its whole length.
171	
172	### Two people
173	
174	The frame holds two faces or two people together when both fit in it. Each box is widened by 15 % before they're tested against the frame. Salient regions aren't paired.
175	
176	## The blurred Backgrounds track
177	
178	Where the frame shows the whole picture, the canvas shows around it. So a blurred copy of the clip goes on a new track named **Backgrounds** at the back, for the clip's whole length. That's the same copy [**Clip ▸ Add Blurred Background**](/canvas/backgrounds/#blurred-background) makes: picture only, filling the canvas.
179	
180	No track is added when no clip needs one. That's always so when Follow or Where Empty is **Center**. Where two selected clips overlap in time, the second copy goes on a further new track behind Backgrounds.
181	
182	A clip with speed actions keeps them on its copy, so the copy shows the same frames.
183	
184	## Every move is an action
185	
186	Every move is an ordinary action on the clip's [action lane](/motion/action-lane/). To nudge where a frame ends, select the action and [drag the picture on the canvas](/motion/edit-an-action/#edit-on-the-canvas). You can [move, resize or remove it](/motion/change-an-action/) as you would any other.
187	
188	## Undo
189	
190	**Edit ▸ Undo Follow Subject** takes the whole command back in one step, every clip and track included. What was found stays in the cache.
191	
192	## Screen recordings are skipped
193	
194	A screen recording Frame Job made, with its [cursor file](/recording/cursor-files/), isn't followed by faces, because a face on a screen isn't what the viewer is looking at. Follow Subject leaves it unanalysed and lists it under the summary:
195	
196	> Clip 3: clip 3's media has a cursor file, so it follows the cursor, not faces; frame it with cursor, center, fit or keep
197	
198	Of those, the sheet offers **Center**. [Make Vertical Version](/framing/make-vertical-version/) follows the pointer instead, and an agent can [follow it too](/framing/reframe-clip/).
199	
200	## Clips it cannot frame
201	
202	A selected movie clip that can't be followed gets a line under the summary, and the others are still framed. With no clip left to frame, the summary shows only those lines and **Follow** stays dimmed.
203	
204	| Clip | The line says | What you can do |
205	| --- | --- | --- |
206	| On a matte track | "clip 3 is on a matte track, which framing would move; only keep reframes it" | Change the track's [matte setting](/canvas/matte-tracks/) or move the clip |
207	| Cut by a matte | "clip 3 is cut by the matte on track 7, which framing would move it out of; only keep reframes it" | The same |
208	| Rotated | "clip 3 is turned 15°, and framing works on an upright picture; only keep reframes it" | Set its [rotation](/canvas/transform/) back to 0° |
209	| Turned by an action | "clip 3's action 12 turns it, and framing works on an upright picture; only keep reframes it" | Take rotation out of [that action](/motion/edit-an-action/#take-a-property-out-of-the-action) |
210	| Spinning | "clip 3 spins in its motion, and framing works on an upright picture; only keep reframes it" | [Clear the spin preset](/motion/motion-presets/#change-or-clear-a-preset) |
211	| Cropped or scaled to nothing | "clip 3's crop or scale leaves no picture to frame" | Fix its [crop](/canvas/crop/) or scale |
212	| With a cursor file | See [above](#screen-recordings-are-skipped) | Choose **Center** |
213	| With no analysis under it | "clip 3 has no subjects to follow; analyze it first" | Lengthen the clip. A clip so short that no sample falls inside it lands here. |
214	
215	"keep" and the other lowercase words in these lines are an agent's options. See [Reframe a clip (agents)](/framing/reframe-clip/).
216	
217	A clip with nobody in it isn't one of these. It's framed on your [Where Empty](#where-empty) choice.
218	
219	When an analysis has to run first, the sheet can't list these lines yet. Afterwards the clips that can be framed are framed, and the rest stay as they were with no message. If none can be, Frame Job beeps and shows the lines at the foot of the inspector.
220	
221	## Good to know
222	
223	- If a selected clip's file is missing or can't be read, the summary says so and **Follow** stays dimmed for all of them. [Relink it](/projects/relink-media/), or choose **Center**, which doesn't read the file.
224	- Follow Subject doesn't frame stills or pictures. [Make Vertical Version](/framing/make-vertical-version/) centres the ones that fill the frame.
225	- Running Follow Subject again on a clip whose frame shows the whole picture adds another Backgrounds track and another copy, and the first copy stays. Undo the first run, or delete the old copy.
226	- Inside a [nest](/editing/nests/), the nest's canvas is the canvas, and the Backgrounds track goes in the nest.
227	- A clip's speed, speed ramps and reversal are all taken into account, so the frame moves with what the clip shows.
228	
229	## With an agent
230	
231	`reframe_clip` frames one clip at a time. Follow Subject is that tool run on each selected clip, starting from the whole picture, with a Backgrounds track behind.
232	
233	An agent has more choices than the sheet. It can show the whole picture, rescale a clip from the canvas it was made for, follow a recorded pointer or follow whoever's talking, and it can compose the framing into a clip's own moves instead of replacing them. See [Reframe a clip (agents)](/framing/reframe-clip/) and [Tools: framing and vertical](/mcp/tools-framing/).
234	
235	## Related
236	
237	- [Subjects in the picture](/framing/what-is-found/)
238	- [Show Subjects](/framing/show-subjects/)
239	- [Make Vertical Version](/framing/make-vertical-version/)
240	- [Backgrounds](/canvas/backgrounds/)
241	- [Actions](/motion/actions/)

<system-reminder>
Contents of /Users/kevingalligan/devel/framejob/.claude/worktrees/help-docs/docs/site/CLAUDE.md:

# CLAUDE.md — the documentation site

The public user documentation: Astro with Starlight, one page per feature or tight family of
features. `pnpm` manages it, and `engines` in `package.json` sets the Node it needs. `README.md` has
the commands.

## Where things are

```
astro.config.mjs        Starlight's settings: title, logo, fonts, theme, plugins
sidebar.mjs             every page's place in the navigation, in order
src/content/docs/       the pages: <section>/<page>.mdx
src/data/features.json  THE FEATURE LIST: what /features/ renders and what the proof reads
src/components/         AtAGlance (a page's facts), Shot (a screen in both looks),
                        FeatureIndex (the filterable list)
src/assets/screens/     WebP captures, written only by scripts/import-screens.mjs
src/styles/             the brand: the mark's inks, the app's faces, square chrome
```

## The rule that matters

**Every claim is written from the code.** A label, a default, a range, a shortcut, a limit or a
refusal is checked against `app/Sources/`, `core/src/`, `graphic/` or `mcp-proxy/` before it is
written, and the code wins over `docs/guide/`, a spec or an ADR. Never write what a feature
probably does. If the code cannot settle it, leave it out.

Nothing dev-only, deferred or unbuilt is documented. That excludes the dev tools (`snapshot_ui`,
`perform_menu_item`, `cancel_sheet`, `select_inspector_tab`, `play_preview`, `graphic_memory`,
`loudness_meter`, `land_recording`, `analysis_job`, `transcript_view`, `playback_rebuilds`,
`assistant_send`, `assistant_answer`) and every `-RCDev` launch default.

## Who reads this

Someone editing a video, who has never read this repository. They want to know what a thing does,
how to do it, and what will stop them. They do not care how it is built.

So a page never mentions: spec or decision IDs (`AU-12`, `§11`), road maps, phases, issue numbers,
source file or type names, `rc_*` exports, format version numbers, proofs, tests, or the history
of a feature. Internal words get translated: "refused" becomes what the user sees ("Frame Job
won't do this while…"), "the core" and "the op" disappear. A tool name is the one exception: the
MCP pages and `tools=` in `AtAGlance` name agent tools, because those are the product's interface.

## Voice

- Plain, direct and second person. Say what it does, then how. Short sentences.
- Open with what the feature is for, in a sentence or two, before any steps.
- British spelling in prose, as `docs/guide/` does (colour, centre, grey, normalise), and the
  app's exact spelling for its own labels (the **Color** tab, **Normalize**).
- Contractions are fine. No marketing: never "powerful", "seamless", "effortless", "robust",
  "simply", "just", "easily", "unleash", "supercharge".
- Prefer a full stop or a comma to an em dash.
- State defaults, ranges and limits as numbers. Say what happens at the edges, because that is
  what a reader comes to a reference for.
- No filler sections. A page with nothing to say under a heading doesn't have that heading.

## Page shape

```mdx
---
title: Markers
description: One sentence, what this page helps you do. Search results show it.
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';

What the feature is for, in a sentence or two.

<AtAGlance menu="Mark ▸ Add Marker" keys="M" tools="add_marker" />

<Shot name="04-editor.window" alt="What the picture shows, for someone who can't see it." />

## Add a marker

<Steps>

1. Move the playhead to the moment.
2. Press <kbd>M</kbd>.

</Steps>

## Options

| Control | What it does | Default |
| ------- | ------------ | ------- |

## Good to know

Limits, edge cases and what stops it, in plain words.

## Related

- [Snapping](/timeline/snapping/)
```

Every section is optional except the opening. Order the task sections as a reader needs them.

- **Headings** start at `##`, are sentence case, and name the job: "Add a marker", not "Adding".
  A feature in `src/data/features.json` with an `anchor` needs a heading that makes that anchor.
- **Menus** are bold with `▸`, spelled as the app spells them: **Clip ▸ Split**.
- **Keys** use the app's symbols in `<kbd>`: <kbd>⌘T</kbd>. Inside `AtAGlance`, pass the string.
- **Controls** are bold where they appear in a step: choose **Save**.
- **Links** are root-absolute with a trailing slash: `/timeline/markers/#add-a-marker`. The build
  fails on a link or anchor that does not exist.
- **Asides** are for what a reader must not miss, not for decoration: `:::note`, `:::tip`,
  `:::caution`, `:::danger`.
- **Screens** come from `src/assets/screens/`. A `name` is the file name without its look and
  extension. Use a screen only when it shows what the page is about, not when the thing is out
  of frame, and give it real alt text.

## MDX traps

MDX is JSX. In prose, `{`, `}` and `<` start code. Put anything like `{x}`, `<1 s` or `a<b` in a
code span, or write it out ("under 1 s"). `<kbd>` and every component must close. A line starting
with `import` or `export` is code. Leave a blank line after an opening component tag and before
its closing tag, or the Markdown inside won't render.

## Checking a page

```sh
node docs/site/scripts/check-pages.mjs <page.mdx>…        # parses, imports, links, captures
python3 tools/proof/docs_site_proof.py --pages <page.mdx>…  # internal words, local paths

```

## Screens

The captures come from the screen catalog (`designs/screens/`, `tools/proof/screens.py`), so the
pictures are of the real app. To refresh them:

```sh
python3 tools/proof/screens.py --out <dir>                      # from the repository root
node docs/site/scripts/import-screens.mjs <dir> --used
```

**This site is public.** `import-screens.mjs` refuses a capture whose layout dump holds a local
path, and its `CROP` table is the only way past that, by cutting the region away. Settings needs
it: its MCP section prints the helper's full path. Never weaken the refusal.

## When the app changes

A user-visible change edits its page here as well as `docs/guide/`, and a new feature adds its row
to `src/data/features.json`. `tools/proof/docs_site_proof.py` runs in `make test` and fails on a
menu item or agent tool the site doesn't document, a feature whose page or anchor is missing, or a
page that names something internal.

612	    /// The Analyzing sheet's answer: refused when the project or scope changed, a failed

614	    private func finishFollow(
615	        _ outcome: AnalyzingSheetController.Outcome, rows: [AnalyzingSheetController.Row],
616	        settings: FollowSubjectSettings, targets: [UInt32], asked: ReelProject, scope: UInt32?,
617	        document: ProjectDocument

619	        guard document.project === asked, document.scope == scope else {
620	            refuseFollow(Self.followChanged, document: document)
621	            return
622	        }
623	        switch outcome {
624	        case .failed(let name, let why):
625	            let request = rows.first { $0.name == name }?.request
626	            let kind = request?.kind.rawValue ?? "framing"
627	            let file = request?.media.name ?? name
628	            refuseFollow("The \(kind) analysis of “\(file)” failed: \(why).", document: document)
629	        case .landed:

633	                    document: document)
634	                return
635	            }
636	            let project = document.editedProject

638	                let subjects = FollowSubject.subjects(targets, in: project, cacheDir: cacheDir)

641	                    guard document.project === asked, document.scope == scope else {

652	    /// The plan on the current handle, as one explicit undo group; nothing framed is refused

658	        let answer: FollowSubject.Answer
659	        do {
660	            answer = try FollowSubject.plan(
661	                targets, subjects: subjects, settings: settings, project: document.editedProject)
662	        } catch {
663	            refuseFollow(error.localizedDescription, document: document)
664	            return

670	            refuseFollow(FollowSubject.summary(plan), document: document)
671	        case .plan(let plan):

673	        }

159	    private func read(
160	        _ kind: AnalysisKind, media: MediaSnapshot, url: URL, urls: [UInt32: URL], cacheDir: URL
161	    ) -> Entry {
162	        let markerURL = AnalysisStore.markerURL(kind, media: media.id, in: cacheDir)
163	        let key = Key(
164	            media: media, url: url, lut: media.color?.lut.flatMap { urls[$0] },
165	            marker: Self.signature(of: markerURL))
166	        if let entry = memo[kind], entry.key == key { return entry }
167	        var entry = Entry(key: key, covered: [], boxes: [])
168	        if key.marker != nil,
169	            let marker = AnalysisStore.readMarker(kind, media: media.id, in: cacheDir),
170	            case let (input, fullRange) = ProjectDocument.analysisInput(
171	                media: media, url: url, urls: urls),
172	            let stamp = AnalysisStamp.make(
173	                kind: kind, media: media, url: url, input: input, fullRange: fullRange),
174	            marker.answers(for: stamp),
175	            let boxes = Self.boxes(kind, media: media.id, cacheDir: cacheDir)
176	        {
177	            entry = Entry(key: key, covered: AnalysisStore.merged(marker.ranges), boxes: boxes)
178	        }
179	        memo[kind] = entry
180	        return entry
181	    }

183	    /// Each sample's boxes and styles; nil when the payload does not decode.
184	    private static func boxes(_ kind: AnalysisKind, media: UInt32, cacheDir: URL)
185	        -> [[(rect: CGRect, style: Style)]]?
186	    {
187	        func rect(_ x: Float, _ y: Float, _ w: Float, _ h: Float) -> CGRect {
188	            CGRect(x: CGFloat(x), y: CGFloat(y), width: CGFloat(w), height: CGFloat(h))
189	        }
190	        switch kind {
191	        case .faces:
192	            guard let data = AnalysisStore.readPayload(
193	                .faces, media: media, file: AnalysisFaces.payloadName, in: cacheDir),
194	                let decoded = AnalysisFaces.decode(data)
195	            else { return nil }
196	            return decoded.samples.map { sample in
197	                sample.faces.map { (rect($0.x, $0.y, $0.width, $0.height), Style.face) }

254	/// What a VR command analyses (spec §11 VR-12; road map "creator-jobs" VR1):
255	/// for each media the named clips show, the windows those clips play plus
256	/// `margin` each side, in the order `kinds` — `shots`, `faces`, `subjects`.
257	/// CJ-20 stands: nothing runs at import; a command wants these requests and
258	/// waits, as Split at Shot Changes does. `reframe_clip`'s tool (VR2a2,
259	/// VR-28), Clip ▸ Follow Subject… (`FollowSubject.swift`, VR-29) and
260	/// `analysis_job {clips}` (dev, the proof's door) call it; View ▸ Show
261	/// Subjects never does (VR-13).
262	///
263	/// Names no `rc_*`; `requests` is main only (it reads the document).
264	enum FramingAnalysis {
265	    /// One second each side of a played window (VR-12).
266	    static let margin: Ticks = 600_000
267	    /// The kinds a framing reads, in the order they are wanted.
268	    static let kinds: [AnalysisKind] = [.shots, .faces, .subjects]
269	
270	    /// One media's windows, in forward-media source ticks [lower, upper),
271	    /// merged where they overlap or touch, in time order.
272	    struct MediaWindows: Equatable {
273	        let media: UInt32
274	        let windows: [ClosedRange<Ticks>]
275	    }
276	
277	    /// Each media clip among `clips` whose media has a moving picture, in
278	    /// order, its media grouped in the order of first appearance; each window
279	    /// the clip's played window (`AnalysisClipTimes`, through its source map,
280	    /// speed and reversal) widened by `margin` each side and clamped to
281	    /// 0…duration, merged per media. Text, shape, graphic, adjustment and nest
282	    /// clips, and clips of an audio file or a still, are skipped.
283	    static func windows(clips: [UInt32], in project: ReelProject) -> [MediaWindows] {
284	        let snapshot = project.snapshot
285	        var order: [UInt32] = []
286	        var found: [UInt32: [ClosedRange<Ticks>]] = [:]
287	        for id in clips {
288	            guard let clip = snapshot.clip(id), qualifies(clip, in: snapshot),
289	                case .media(let mediaID, _, _) = clip.source, let media = snapshot.media(mediaID)
290	            else { continue }
291	            let played = AnalysisClipTimes(clip: clip, media: media, map: project.sourceMap(id))
292	                .window
293	            let lower = max(0, played.lowerBound - margin)
294	            let upper = min(max(0, media.duration), played.upperBound + margin)
295	            guard lower <= upper else { continue }
296	            if found[mediaID] == nil { order.append(mediaID) }
297	            found[mediaID, default: []].append(lower...upper)
298	        }
299	        return order.map { MediaWindows(media: $0, windows: merged(found[$0] ?? [])) }
300	    }
301	
302	    /// Whether `clip` is one `windows` reads: a media clip whose media is a
303	    /// video with a moving picture (spec §11 VR-29 (a)).
304	    static func qualifies(_ clip: ClipSnapshot, in snapshot: ProjectSnapshot) -> Bool {
305	        guard case .media(let mediaID, _, _) = clip.source, let media = snapshot.media(mediaID)
306	        else { return false }
307	        return media.kind == .video && media.hasVideo
308	    }
309	
310	    /// Every request `kinds` need over `windows(clips:in:)` of `project` —
311	    /// the document's open scope when nil, else the container a call named
312	    /// (`reframe_clip`'s, spec §11 VR-28): kind-major in `kinds` order, then
313	    /// media in the windows' order, each kind's need the windows' grid indices
314	    /// widened by its read margin
315	    /// (`ProjectDocument.analysisRequest(kind:media:url:urls:cacheDir:need:)`);
316	    /// a hit is omitted. Throws the request's own errors (a missing file, no
317	    /// cache folder, an unreadable file). Main thread.
318	    static func requests(
319	        clips: [UInt32], in document: ProjectDocument, project: ReelProject? = nil
320	    ) throws -> [AnalysisRequest] {
321	        let project = project ?? document.editedProject
322	        let all = windows(clips: clips, in: project)
323	        guard !all.isEmpty else { return [] }
324	        let urls = document.mediaURLs()
325	        guard let cacheDir = document.cacheDirectory else {
326	            throw ProjectDocument.AnalysisRequestError.noCache
327	        }
328	        var requests: [AnalysisRequest] = []
329	        for kind in kinds {
330	            for entry in all {
331	                guard let media = project.snapshot.media(entry.media) else { continue }
332	                guard let url = urls[entry.media] else {
333	                    throw ProjectDocument.AnalysisRequestError.missingFile(entry.media)
334	                }
335	                let grid = kind.grid(of: media)
336	                let need = entry.windows.compactMap {
337	                    grid.indices(from: $0.lowerBound, to: $0.upperBound)
338	                }.map { grid.need($0, margin: kind.margin) }
339	                guard !need.isEmpty else { continue }
340	                if let request = try ProjectDocument.analysisRequest(
341	                    kind: kind, media: media, url: url, urls: urls, cacheDir: cacheDir,
342	                    need: need)
343	                {
344	                    requests.append(request)
345	                }
346	            }
347	        }
348	        return requests
349	    }
350	
351	    /// Tick ranges merged where they overlap or touch, in order.
352	    static func merged(_ ranges: [ClosedRange<Ticks>]) -> [ClosedRange<Ticks>] {
353	        var out: [ClosedRange<Ticks>] = []
354	        for range in ranges.sorted(by: { $0.lowerBound < $1.lowerBound }) {
355	            if let last = out.last, range.lowerBound <= last.upperBound {
356	                out[out.count - 1] = last.lowerBound...max(last.upperBound, range.upperBound)
357	            } else {
358	                out.append(range)
359	            }
360	        }
361	        return out
362	    }
363	}

368	/// strict reader takes, `{samples: [{t, faces, people, salient}], shots: [t]}`

371	/// mouth gap over its width, SW-81's opening — when both were read, the width
372	/// is above 0 and the gap at least 0 (VR6a, spec §11 VR-60 (b)); only
373	/// `follow: speaker` reads it.

375	/// - **Samples.** The `faces` grid (VR-11), which `subjects` shares: each
376	///   index inside `windows` that BOTH kinds' markers cover is one sample at
377	///   `grid.ticks(of: k)`, with that index's faces, people and salient boxes.
378	/// - **Boxes.** Each is clamped into the picture and dropped when no area is
379	///   left — Vision's edge faces reach outside 0…1, and the core refuses a
380	///   coordinate there — and each kind keeps its first `maxBoxes` in stored
381	///   order (CJ-31's).
382	/// - **Shots.** `AnalysisShots.cuts` over each window's indices that the
383	///   `shots` marker covers, answered as each cut's frame pts.

388	    /// The most boxes of a kind per sample: the core's `MAX_SUBJECT_BOXES`.

391	    static func read(media: MediaSnapshot, windows: [ClosedRange<Ticks>], cacheDir: URL)
392	        -> [String: Any]
393	    {
394	        let grid = AnalysisKind.faces.grid(of: media)
395	        let facesMarker = AnalysisStore.readMarker(.faces, media: media.id, in: cacheDir)
396	        let subjectsMarker = AnalysisStore.readMarker(.subjects, media: media.id, in: cacheDir)
397	        let faces = payload(.faces, facesMarker, media, cacheDir)
398	            .flatMap(AnalysisFaces.decode)?.samples ?? []
399	        let subjects = payload(.subjects, subjectsMarker, media, cacheDir)
400	            .flatMap(AnalysisSubjects.decode)?.samples ?? []
401	        let both = (facesMarker?.ranges ?? [], subjectsMarker?.ranges ?? [])
402	        var samples: [[String: Any]] = []
403	        for window in windows {
404	            guard let indices = grid.indices(from: window.lowerBound, to: window.upperBound)
405	            else { continue }
406	            for k in indices where holds(both.0, k) && holds(both.1, k) {
407	                var sample: [String: Any] = ["t": grid.ticks(of: k)]
408	                let found = k < faces.count ? faces[k].faces : []
409	                sample["faces"] = boxes(
410	                    found.map { ($0.x, $0.y, $0.width, $0.height, $0.confidence) },
411	                    mouths: found.map(mouth))
412	                let there = k < subjects.count ? subjects[k].subjects : .init(people: [], salient: [])
413	                sample["people"] = boxes(there.people.map {
414	                    ($0.x, $0.y, $0.width, $0.height, $0.confidence)
415	                })
416	                sample["salient"] = boxes(there.salient.map {
417	                    ($0.x, $0.y, $0.width, $0.height, $0.confidence)
418	                })
419	                samples.append(sample)
420	            }
421	        }
422	        return ["samples": samples, "shots": shots(media: media, windows: windows, cacheDir)]
423	    }

425	    /// Each cut's pts among the windows' indices the `shots` marker covers,
426	    /// ascending, once each.
427	    private static func shots(media: MediaSnapshot, windows: [ClosedRange<Ticks>], _ cacheDir: URL)
428	        -> [Ticks]
429	    {
430	        let grid = AnalysisKind.shots.grid(of: media)
431	        let marker = AnalysisStore.readMarker(.shots, media: media.id, in: cacheDir)
432	        guard let marker, let data = payload(.shots, marker, media, cacheDir) else { return [] }
433	        let records = AnalysisShots.decode(data, count: grid.count)
434	        var found = Set<Ticks>()
435	        for window in windows {
436	            guard let indices = grid.indices(from: window.lowerBound, to: window.upperBound)
437	            else { continue }
438	            for covered in marker.ranges where covered.overlaps(indices) {
439	                let piece = max(covered.lowerBound, indices.lowerBound)...min(
440	                    covered.upperBound, indices.upperBound)
441	                for k in AnalysisShots.cuts(records, in: piece) where k < records.count {
442	                    found.insert(records[k].pts)
443	                }
444	            }
445	        }
446	        return found.sorted()
447	    }

449	    /// The kind's first payload file, as the marker names it.
450	    private static func payload(
451	        _ kind: AnalysisKind, _ marker: AnalysisMarker?, _ media: MediaSnapshot, _ cacheDir: URL
452	    ) -> Data? {
453	        guard let file = marker?.files.first else { return nil }
454	        return AnalysisStore.readPayload(kind, media: media.id, file: file, in: cacheDir)
455	    }
456	
457	    private static func holds(_ ranges: [ClosedRange<Int>], _ k: Int) -> Bool {
458	        ranges.contains { $0.contains(k) }
459	    }

461	    /// A face's mouth gap over its width; nil when either is unread, the width
462	    /// is not above 0 or the gap is below 0 (VR-60 (b)).
463	    static func mouth(_ face: AnalysisFaces.Face) -> Double? {
464	        let gap = Double(face.mouthGap), width = Double(face.mouthWidth)
465	        guard gap.isFinite, width.isFinite, width > 0, gap >= 0 else { return nil }
466	        return gap / width
467	    }
468	
469	    /// Boxes clamped into the picture, the empty ones dropped, the first
470	    /// `maxBoxes` kept; a face's `mouth` when `mouths` gives one.
471	    private static func boxes(
472	        _ raw: [(Float, Float, Float, Float, Float)], mouths: [Double?] = []
473	    ) -> [[String: Any]] {
474	        var out: [[String: Any]] = []
475	        for (index, (x, y, w, h, c)) in raw.enumerated() {
476	            let values = [x, y, w, h, c].map(Double.init)
477	            guard values.allSatisfy(\.isFinite) else { continue }
478	            let (x0, y0) = (max(0, values[0]), max(0, values[1]))
479	            let (x1, y1) = (min(1, values[0] + values[2]), min(1, values[1] + values[3]))
480	            guard x1 > x0, y1 > y0 else { continue }
481	            var box: [String: Any] = [
482	                "x": x0, "y": y0, "w": x1 - x0, "h": y1 - y0, "c": min(1, max(0, values[4])),
483	            ]
484	            if index < mouths.count, let mouth = mouths[index] { box["mouth"] = mouth }
485	            out.append(box)
486	            if out.count == maxBoxes { break }
487	        }
488	        return out
489	    }

642	        guard boxHeight > 0,
643	            let inner = face.landmarks?.innerLips?.pointsInImage(imageSize: size),
644	            let outer = face.landmarks?.outerLips?.pointsInImage(imageSize: size),
645	            let top = inner.map(\.y).max(), let bottom = inner.map(\.y).min(),
646	            let right = outer.map(\.x).max(), let left = outer.map(\.x).min()
647	        else { return (.nan, .nan) }
648	        return (Float((top - bottom) / boxHeight), Float((right - left) / boxHeight))

653	    /// interval` (`previous` the kept frame before it, nil at the media's

655	    static func samples(at pts: Int64, after previous: Int64?, grid: AnalysisGrid)
656	        -> ClosedRange<Int>?
657	    {
658	        let after = previous ?? Int64.min
659	        let upto = pts
660	        var high = min(grid.lastIndex, Int((Double(upto) * grid.rate).rounded(.down)) + 1)
661	        while high >= 0, grid.ticks(of: high) > upto { high -= 1 }
662	        var low = high + 1
663	        while low > 0 {
664	            let t = grid.ticks(of: low - 1)
665	            guard t > after, Double(pts) < Double(t) + grid.frameTicks else { break }
666	            low -= 1
667	        }
668	        return low <= high ? low...high : nil

697	/// `samples.bin` (spec §11 CJ-33; road map "creator-jobs" CJ3), the `faces`
698	/// kind's one payload file per media, little-endian:
699	///
700	/// - a 16-byte header: ASCII `FJFS`, `UInt16` version 1, `UInt16` face record
701	///   bytes (36, or 28 without landmarks), `UInt32` sample count, `UInt32` face
702	///   count;
703	/// - one 16-byte row per sample index from 0: `Int64` the frame's pts in
704	///   ticks (−1: no frame), `UInt32` its first face, `UInt32` its face count;
705	/// - the face records: `Float32` x, y, width, height (0…1, top-left, display
706	///   orientation), confidence, roll, yaw (radians), and with landmarks mouth
707	///   gap and mouth width (NaN: absent).
708	///
709	/// The cache is raw; only the answer rounds. A publish decodes the on-disk
710	/// file and replaces the samples it covers; a file that does not decode, or
711	/// holds another sample count or record size, is written fresh and answers
712	/// false, so the store keeps the job's coverage alone.
713	extension AnalysisFaces {
714	
715	    static let fileVersion: UInt16 = 1
716	    static var recordBytes: UInt16 { landmarks ? 36 : 28 }
717	    static let headerBytes = 16
718	    static let rowBytes = 16
719	
720	    /// One face as stored; NaN marks an absent value. Equal bit for bit.
721	    struct Face: Equatable {
722	        var x, y, width, height, confidence, roll, yaw, mouthGap, mouthWidth: Float
723	
724	        var values: [Float] { [x, y, width, height, confidence, roll, yaw, mouthGap, mouthWidth] }
725	
726	        static func == (a: Face, b: Face) -> Bool {
727	            a.values.map(\.bitPattern) == b.values.map(\.bitPattern)
728	        }
729	    }
730	
731	    /// One sample: the frame it read (pts −1: none) and its faces in CJ-31's order.
732	    struct Sample: Equatable {
733	        var pts: Int64
734	        var faces: [Face]
735	
736	        static let empty = Sample(pts: -1, faces: [])
737	    }
738	
739	    /// nil when `data` is not a `samples.bin` this build reads.
740	    static func decode(_ data: Data) -> (count: Int, samples: [Sample])? {
741	        guard data.count >= headerBytes else { return nil }
742	        let bytes = [UInt8](data)
743	        func u16(_ at: Int) -> UInt16 { UInt16(bytes[at]) | UInt16(bytes[at + 1]) << 8 }
744	        func u32(_ at: Int) -> UInt32 {
745	            (0..<4).reduce(UInt32(0)) { $0 | UInt32(bytes[at + $1]) << (8 * UInt32($1)) }
746	        }
747	        func i64(_ at: Int) -> Int64 {
748	            Int64(bitPattern: (0..<8).reduce(UInt64(0)) { $0 | UInt64(bytes[at + $1]) << (8 * UInt64($1)) })
749	        }
750	        guard bytes[0..<4].elementsEqual(Array("FJFS".utf8)), u16(4) == fileVersion else {
751	            return nil
752	        }
753	        let record = Int(u16(6))
754	        guard record == 36 || record == 28 else { return nil }
755	        let count = Int(u32(8)), faceCount = Int(u32(12))
756	        let facesAt = headerBytes + count * rowBytes
757	        guard data.count == facesAt + faceCount * record else { return nil }
758	        var faces: [Face] = []
759	        faces.reserveCapacity(faceCount)
760	        for i in 0..<faceCount {
761	            let at = facesAt + i * record
762	            var v = (0..<(record / 4)).map { Float(bitPattern: u32(at + $0 * 4)) }
763	            if v.count == 7 { v += [.nan, .nan] }
764	            faces.append(
765	                Face(x: v[0], y: v[1], width: v[2], height: v[3], confidence: v[4], roll: v[5],
766	                     yaw: v[6], mouthGap: v[7], mouthWidth: v[8]))
767	        }
768	        var samples: [Sample] = []
769	        samples.reserveCapacity(count)
770	        for k in 0..<count {
771	            let at = headerBytes + k * rowBytes
772	            let first = Int(u32(at + 8)), n = Int(u32(at + 12))
773	            guard first + n <= faceCount else { return nil }
774	            samples.append(Sample(pts: i64(at), faces: Array(faces[first..<(first + n)])))
775	        }
776	        return (count, samples)
777	    }
778	
779	    /// The bytes of `samples`, at this build's record size.
780	    static func encode(_ samples: [Sample]) -> Data {
781	        var data = Data()
782	        let faceCount = samples.reduce(0) { $0 + $1.faces.count }
783	        data.reserveCapacity(headerBytes + samples.count * rowBytes + faceCount * Int(recordBytes))
784	        func put<T: FixedWidthInteger>(_ value: T) {
785	            withUnsafeBytes(of: value.littleEndian) { data.append(contentsOf: $0) }
786	        }
787	        data.append(contentsOf: Array("FJFS".utf8))
788	        put(fileVersion)
789	        put(recordBytes)
790	        put(UInt32(samples.count))
791	        put(UInt32(faceCount))
792	        var first = 0
793	        for sample in samples {
794	            put(sample.pts)
795	            put(UInt32(first))
796	            put(UInt32(sample.faces.count))
797	            first += sample.faces.count
798	        }
799	        let fields = Int(recordBytes) / 4
800	        for face in samples.flatMap(\.faces) {
801	            for value in face.values.prefix(fields) { put(value.bitPattern) }
802	        }
803	        return data
804	    }
805	
806	    /// The publish's write: the on-disk file decoded (when it answers for the
807	    /// stamp and decodes at `count` samples and this record size) with
808	    /// `covering`'s samples replaced by `samples` (absent: `Sample.empty`),
809	    /// else a fresh file of `count` samples; written to `partial`. Answers
810	    /// whether it merged.
811	    static func write(
812	        onDisk: URL?, partial: URL, count: Int, covering: ClosedRange<Int>,
813	        samples: [Int: Sample]
814	    ) throws -> Bool {
815	        var merged = false
816	        var all = [Sample](repeating: .empty, count: count)
817	        if let onDisk, let data = try? Data(contentsOf: onDisk), let old = decode(data),
818	            old.count == count, data.count >= 8,
819	            UInt16(data[data.startIndex + 6]) | UInt16(data[data.startIndex + 7]) << 8
820	                == recordBytes
821	        {
822	            all = old.samples
823	            merged = true
824	        }
825	        for k in covering where k >= 0 && k < count { all[k] = samples[k] ?? .empty }
826	        try encode(all).write(to: partial)
827	        return merged
828	    }
829	}

994	
995	    static let fileVersion: UInt16 = 1
996	    static let recordBytes: UInt16 = 20
997	    static let headerBytes = 16
998	    static let rowBytes = 16
999	
1000	    /// One box as stored. Equal bit for bit.
1001	    struct Box: Equatable {
1002	        var x, y, width, height, confidence: Float
1003	
1004	        var values: [Float] { [x, y, width, height, confidence] }
1005	
1006	        static func == (a: Box, b: Box) -> Bool {
1007	            a.values.map(\.bitPattern) == b.values.map(\.bitPattern)

1010	
1011	    /// What one analysed frame holds: its people and its salient regions.
1012	    struct Subjects: Equatable {

1014	        var salient: [Box]
1015	    }

1018	    struct Sample: Equatable {

1026	    static func ordered(_ boxes: [Box]) -> [Box] {

1028	            let ax = a.x + a.width / 2, bx = b.x + b.width / 2

1039	        func u32(_ at: Int) -> UInt32 {
1040	            (0..<4).reduce(UInt32(0)) { $0 | UInt32(bytes[at + $1]) << (8 * UInt32($1)) }
1041	        }

1082	        put(recordBytes)

85	    /// VR-29 (b): 1 (fill, the owner's answer), or 1.25 when the first clip's media is within
86	    /// 1 % of the canvas's aspect.
87	    static func defaultZoom(_ clips: [UInt32], in snapshot: ProjectSnapshot) -> Double {
88	        guard let first = clips.first, let clip = snapshot.clip(first),
89	            let media = snapshot.media(for: clip), media.width > 0, media.height > 0,
90	            snapshot.canvas.width > 0, snapshot.canvas.height > 0
91	        else { return 1 }
92	        let picture = Double(media.width) / Double(media.height)
93	        let canvas = Double(snapshot.canvas.width) / Double(snapshot.canvas.height)
94	        return abs(picture / canvas - 1) <= 0.01 ? 1.25 : 1

98	    /// VR-51). A clip whose media has one stays a target, so the core's VR-51 sentence is
99	    /// listed as its refusal, but it is never requested or read.
100	    static func analysed(_ clips: [UInt32], in project: ReelProject) -> [UInt32] {
101	        let snapshot = project.snapshot
102	        return clips.filter { id in
103	            snapshot.clip(id).flatMap { snapshot.media(for: $0) }?.cursor == nil

108	    /// `reframe_clip`'s tool reads them; a clip whose media has a cursor file is skipped
109	    /// (`analysed`, VR-51). Reads files only: any thread.
110	    static func subjects(_ clips: [UInt32], in project: ReelProject, cacheDir: URL)
111	        -> [UInt32: [String: Any]]
112	    {
113	        var out: [UInt32: [String: Any]] = [:]
114	        for clip in analysed(clips, in: project) {
115	            guard let entry = FramingAnalysis.windows(clips: [clip], in: project).first,
116	                let media = project.snapshot.media(entry.media)
117	            else { continue }
118	            out[clip] = FramingSubjects.read(
119	                media: media, windows: entry.windows, cacheDir: cacheDir)

124	    /// VR-29 (e) on `project`, the handle of the container being edited. Throws only the core's
125	    /// invalid input.
126	    static func plan(
127	        _ clips: [UInt32], subjects: [UInt32: [String: Any]], settings: FollowSubjectSettings,
128	        project: ReelProject
129	    ) throws -> Answer {
130	        var trial = SwitchAngle.Trial(project: project)
131	        let known = Set(project.snapshot.tracks.map(\.id))
132	        if let why = try trial.require(.addTrack(index: 0, name: backgroundsName)) {
133	            return .refused("Follow Subject was refused at add_track: \(why)")
134	        }
135	        guard let track = trial.project.snapshot.tracks.first(where: { !known.contains($0.id) })
136	        else { return .refused("Follow Subject was refused at add_track: no track was added.") }
137	
138	        var framed: [UInt32] = []
139	        var unchanged: [UInt32] = []
140	        var refused: [(clip: UInt32, reason: String)] = []
141	        var moreTracks = 0
142	        var reEased = 0
143	        var carried = 0
144	        for clip in clips {
145	            let op = settings.op(clip: clip, backdrop: track.id, subjects: subjects[clip])
146	            let prior = trial.project
147	            switch try prior.applying(op) {
148	            case .applied(let next):
149	                trial.project = next
150	                trial.ops.append(op)
151	                framed.append(clip)
152	                moreTracks += next.snapshot.tracks.count - prior.snapshot.tracks.count
153	                let counted = counts(before: prior, after: next, clip: clip)
154	                reEased += counted.reEased
155	                carried += counted.carried
156	            case .identity:
157	                unchanged.append(clip)
158	            case .refused(let refusal):
159	                refused.append((clip, refusal.reason))
160	            }
161	        }
162	        guard !framed.isEmpty else {
163	            return .plan(
164	                Plan(
165	                    ops: [], framed: [], unchanged: unchanged, refused: refused,
166	                    backgrounds: false, moreTracks: 0, reEased: 0, carried: 0))
167	        }
168	        let backgrounds = !trial.project.snapshot.clips(onTrack: track.id).isEmpty
169	        if !backgrounds, let why = try trial.require(.removeTrack(track: track.id)) {
170	            return .refused("Follow Subject was refused at remove_track: \(why)")
171	        }
172	        return .plan(
173	            Plan(
174	                ops: trial.ops, framed: framed, unchanged: unchanged, refused: refused,
175	                backgrounds: backgrounds, moreTracks: moreTracks, reEased: reEased,
176	                carried: carried))
177	    }
178	
179	    /// VR-27 (f), for `clip` between two handles of its container: re-eased, an action in both
180	    /// whose duration shrank and whose after curve is not linear; carried, an action with the
181	    /// same id and span in both across which — under `replace` — the AFTER handle's video
182	    /// scale, x or y differs by more than 1e-6, or — composed (`replace: false`, Make
183	    /// Vertical's step, spec §11 VR-34) — the framing F (`framing`) differs by more than 1e-6
184	    /// between the action's two ends.
185	    static func counts(
186	        before: ReelProject, after: ReelProject, clip: UInt32, replace: Bool = true
187	    ) -> (reEased: Int, carried: Int) {
188	        guard let old = before.snapshot.clip(clip), let new = after.snapshot.clip(clip) else {
189	            return (0, 0)
190	        }
191	        var reEased = 0
192	        var carried = 0
193	        for action in new.actions {
194	            guard let was = old.actions.first(where: { $0.id == action.id }) else { continue }
195	            if action.duration < was.duration, action.curve != .linear { reEased += 1 }
196	            guard action.start == was.start, action.duration == was.duration else { continue }
197	            let (a, b) = (new.start + action.start, new.start + action.endTime)
198	            let from: [Double]?
199	            let to: [Double]?
200	            if replace {
201	                from = placement(after, clip, at: a)
202	                to = placement(after, clip, at: b)
203	            } else {
204	                from = framing(before: before, after: after, clip: clip, at: a)
205	                    .map { [$0.k, $0.dx, $0.dy] }
206	                to = framing(before: before, after: after, clip: clip, at: b)
207	                    .map { [$0.k, $0.dx, $0.dy] }
208	            }
209	            if let from, let to, zip(from, to).contains(where: { abs($0 - $1) > 1e-6 }) {
210	                carried += 1
211	            }
212	        }
213	        return (reEased, carried)
214	    }

216	    /// The framing F at project time `t` from both handles' evaluated video (spec §11 VR-34):
217	    /// k = s′/s, dx = x′ − k·x, dy = y′ − k·y; nil when either answers no video or s is 0.
218	    static func framing(before: ReelProject, after: ReelProject, clip: UInt32, at t: Ticks)
219	        -> (k: Double, dx: Double, dy: Double)?
220	    {
221	        guard let was = placement(before, clip, at: t), let now = placement(after, clip, at: t),
222	            was[0] != 0
223	        else { return nil }
224	        let k = now[0] / was[0]
225	        return (k, now[1] - k * was[1], now[2] - k * was[2])
226	    }
227	
228	    /// The clip's evaluated video (scale, x, y) at project time `t`; nil when the core answers
229	    /// no video group.
230	    private static func placement(_ project: ReelProject, _ clip: UInt32, at t: Ticks)
231	        -> [Double]?
232	    {
233	        guard let video = project.clipState(clip, at: t)?["video"] as? [String: Any] else {
234	            return nil
235	        }
236	        func value(_ key: String, _ fallback: Double) -> Double {
237	            (video[key] as? NSNumber)?.doubleValue ?? fallback
238	        }
239	        return [value("scale", 1), value("x", 0), value("y", 0)]
240	    }

242	    /// VR-29 (g): the counts, then one line per clip already framed or refused. With nothing
243	    /// framed, only the lines.
244	    static func summary(_ plan: Plan) -> String {
245	        var lines: [String] = []
246	        if !plan.framed.isEmpty {
247	            var text = "Frames \(counted(plan.framed.count, "clip"))."
248	            if plan.backgrounds { text += " Adds a Backgrounds track for the blurred copy." }
249	            if plan.moreTracks > 0 {
250	                text += " Adds \(plan.moreTracks) more \(plan.moreTracks == 1 ? "track" : "tracks")"
251	                    + " behind it where clips overlap."
252	            }
253	            if plan.reEased > 0 { text += " \(counted(plan.reEased, "action")) re-eased at a cut." }
254	            if plan.carried > 0 {
255	                text += " \(counted(plan.carried, "action")) "
256	                    + (plan.carried == 1 ? "carries" : "carry") + " a framing move."
257	            }
258	            lines.append(text)
259	        }
260	        lines += plan.unchanged.map { "Clip \($0) is already framed this way." }
261	        lines += plan.refused.map { "Clip \($0.clip): \($0.reason)" }
262	        return lines.joined(separator: "\n")
263	    }

267	        "Finds the faces, people and shot changes in \(counted(files, "file")) on this Mac "
268	            + "first, then frames \(counted(clips, "clip"))."

284	        "\(n) \(noun)\(n == 1 ? "" : "s")"
285	    }

612	    /// The Analyzing sheet's answer: refused when the project or scope changed, a failed
613	    /// analysis named; else the subjects read off main and the plan committed.
614	    private func finishFollow(
615	        _ outcome: AnalyzingSheetController.Outcome, rows: [AnalyzingSheetController.Row],
616	        settings: FollowSubjectSettings, targets: [UInt32], asked: ReelProject, scope: UInt32?,
617	        document: ProjectDocument
618	    ) {
619	        guard document.project === asked, document.scope == scope else {
620	            refuseFollow(Self.followChanged, document: document)
621	            return
622	        }
623	        switch outcome {
624	        case .failed(let name, let why):
625	            let request = rows.first { $0.name == name }?.request
626	            let kind = request?.kind.rawValue ?? "framing"
627	            let file = request?.media.name ?? name
628	            refuseFollow("The \(kind) analysis of “\(file)” failed: \(why).", document: document)
629	        case .landed:
630	            guard let cacheDir = document.cacheDirectory else {
631	                refuseFollow(
632	                    ProjectDocument.AnalysisRequestError.noCache.localizedDescription,
633	                    document: document)
634	                return
635	            }
636	            let project = document.editedProject
637	            DispatchQueue.global(qos: .userInitiated).async { [weak self, weak document] in
638	                let subjects = FollowSubject.subjects(targets, in: project, cacheDir: cacheDir)
639	                DispatchQueue.main.async {
640	                    guard let self, let document else { return }
641	                    guard document.project === asked, document.scope == scope else {
642	                        self.refuseFollow(Self.followChanged, document: document)
643	                        return
644	                    }
645	                    self.commitFollow(
646	                        targets, subjects: subjects, settings: settings, document: document)
647	                }
648	            }
649	        }
650	    }

652	    /// The plan on the current handle, as one explicit undo group; nothing framed is refused
653	    /// with the summary's lines.
654	    private func commitFollow(
655	        _ targets: [UInt32], subjects: [UInt32: [String: Any]], settings: FollowSubjectSettings,
656	        document: ProjectDocument
657	    ) {
658	        let answer: FollowSubject.Answer
659	        do {
660	            answer = try FollowSubject.plan(
661	                targets, subjects: subjects, settings: settings, project: document.editedProject)
662	        } catch {
663	            refuseFollow(error.localizedDescription, document: document)
664	            return
665	        }
666	        switch answer {
667	        case .refused(let why):
668	            refuseFollow(why, document: document)
669	        case .plan(let plan) where plan.ops.isEmpty:
670	            refuseFollow(FollowSubject.summary(plan), document: document)
671	        case .plan(let plan):
672	            document.performGroupedEdit(FollowSubject.actionName, plan.ops)
673	        }
674	    }

3	/// View ▸ Show Subjects' drawing (spec §11 VR-13; road map "creator-jobs"
4	/// VR1): the selected clip's cached face, person and salient boxes at the
5	/// playhead, over the canvas. One per window while the item is on (the
6	/// canvas's `subjects`), never persisted.
7	///
8	/// **It draws only what is cached and never starts a job**: it never calls
9	/// `analysisRequest`, `AnalysisLane.want` or `cacheDirectory` (which would
10	/// create the folder); it reads markers and payloads under the document's
11	/// `intendedCacheDirectory`.
12	///
13	/// **Which sample.** The canvas's primary box, when its clip is a media clip
14	/// of a video media: the playhead's forward source tick through the clip's
15	/// source map and the reversed mirror (`sourceTick`, `TimelineView.sourceTime`,
16	/// `ReverseMirror`), then the kind's sample index (`sampleIndex`). A kind
17	/// draws only when that index is covered by a marker that answers for the
18	/// stamp `ProjectDocument.analysisRequest` would make.
19	///
20	/// **The memo** (CO-25's key, as `CutoutMasks`'): per kind, the marker's
21	/// (inode, size, mtime), the media, its URL and its LUT's URL; the marker, the
22	/// stamp check and the payload are read again only when one changes, and an
23	/// `.analysisDidPublish` of `faces` or `subjects` in the document's cache
24	/// folder drops the memo and redraws.
25	///
26	/// **Where.** Each box is placed in the layer's uncropped rectangle, turned
27	/// with the layer (`corners`, ProjectSnapshot's (★) through `CanvasLayerBox`),
28	/// and clipped to the layer's cropped corners. Faces in `DS.snapGuide`, people
29	/// in teal, salient regions in purple dashed, each over a black backing
30	/// stroke as the selection outline has. With neither kind covering, "Not
31	/// analyzed" at the layer's top-left corner. Main only.
32	final class SubjectsOverlay {
33	    static let notAnalyzed = "Not analyzed — Clip ▸ Follow Subject… analyzes it"
34	    /// The kinds drawn, back to front.
35	    static let kinds: [AnalysisKind] = [.subjects, .faces]
36	
37	    private weak var document: ProjectDocument?
38	    private let redraw: () -> Void
39	    private var observer: NSObjectProtocol?
40	    private var memo: [AnalysisKind: Entry] = [:]
41	
42	    /// What a kind's read depends on (CO-25).
43	    private struct Key: Equatable {
44	        let media: MediaSnapshot
45	        let url: URL
46	        let lut: URL?
47	        let marker: Signature?
48	    }
49	
50	    private struct Signature: Equatable {
51	        let inode: UInt64
52	        let size: Int64
53	        let seconds: Int
54	        let nanoseconds: Int
55	    }
56	
57	    /// One kind's read: its covered ranges and boxes per sample (nil: no
58	    /// marker answering for the stamp).
59	    private struct Entry {
60	        let key: Key
61	        let covered: [ClosedRange<Int>]
62	        let boxes: [[(rect: CGRect, style: Style)]]
63	    }
64	
65	    private enum Style { case face, person, salient }
66	
67	    init(document: ProjectDocument, redraw: @escaping () -> Void) {
68	        self.document = document
69	        self.redraw = redraw
70	        observer = NotificationCenter.default.addObserver(
71	            forName: .analysisDidPublish, object: nil, queue: .main
72	        ) { [weak self] note in
73	            MainActor.assumeIsolated { self?.didPublish(note) }
74	        }
75	    }

78	        if let observer { NotificationCenter.default.removeObserver(observer) }
79	    }

81	    private func didPublish(_ note: Notification) {
82	        guard let kind = note.userInfo?["kind"] as? String,
83	            kind == AnalysisKind.faces.rawValue || kind == AnalysisKind.subjects.rawValue,
84	            let folder = note.userInfo?["cacheDir"] as? String,
85	            folder == document?.intendedCacheDirectory?.standardizedFileURL.path

91	    // MARK: - Drawing
92	
93	    func draw(on canvas: PreviewCanvasView) {
94	        guard let document, let layer = canvas.primaryBox,
95	            case .media(let id, _, _) = layer.clip.source,
96	            let media = canvas.snapshot.media(id), media.kind == .video, media.hasVideo
97	        else { return }
98	        let urls = document.mediaURLs()
99	        guard let url = urls[id], let cacheDir = document.intendedCacheDirectory else {
100	            label(on: canvas, layer: layer)
101	            return
102	        }
103	        let source = Self.sourceTick(
104	            of: layer.clip, in: media, at: canvas.playhead,
105	            map: canvas.project?.sourceMap(layer.clip.id))
106	        var drew = false
107	        NSGraphicsContext.saveGraphicsState()
108	        canvas.polygon(layer.corners).addClip()
109	        for kind in Self.kinds {
110	            let entry = read(kind, media: media, url: url, urls: urls, cacheDir: cacheDir)
111	            let k = Self.sampleIndex(at: source, grid: kind.grid(of: media))
112	            guard entry.covered.contains(where: { $0.contains(k) }), k < entry.boxes.count
113	            else { continue }
114	            drew = true
115	            for (rect, style) in entry.boxes[k] {
116	                stroke(canvas.polygon(Self.corners(of: rect, on: layer)), style)
117	            }
118	        }
119	        NSGraphicsContext.restoreGraphicsState()
120	        if !drew { label(on: canvas, layer: layer) }
121	    }

123	    private func stroke(_ path: NSBezierPath, _ style: Style) {
124	        NSColor.black.withAlphaComponent(0.4).setStroke()
125	        path.lineWidth = 2
126	        path.stroke()
127	        switch style {
128	        case .face: DS.snapGuide.setStroke()
129	        case .person: NSColor.systemTeal.setStroke()
130	        case .salient:
131	            NSColor.systemPurple.setStroke()
132	            let dash: [CGFloat] = [4, 3]
133	            path.setLineDash(dash, count: dash.count, phase: 0)
134	        }
135	        path.lineWidth = 1
136	        path.stroke()
137	    }

139	    /// "Not analyzed" at the layer's top-left corner, on a dark backing.
140	    private func label(on canvas: PreviewCanvasView, layer: CanvasLayerBox) {
141	        guard let corner = layer.corners.first else { return }
142	        let at = canvas.canvasToView(corner)
143	        let text = NSAttributedString(
144	            string: Self.notAnalyzed,
145	            attributes: [
146	                .font: NSFont.systemFont(ofSize: 11, weight: .medium),
147	                .foregroundColor: NSColor.white,
148	            ])
149	        let size = text.size()
150	        let y = canvas.overlay.isFlipped ? at.y + 4 : at.y - 4 - size.height
151	        let box = CGRect(x: at.x + 4, y: y, width: size.width + 8, height: size.height + 2)
152	        NSColor.black.withAlphaComponent(0.55).setFill()
153	        NSBezierPath(rect: box).fill()
154	        text.draw(at: CGPoint(x: box.minX + 4, y: box.minY + 1))
155	    }

157	    // MARK: - The read
158	
159	    private func read(
160	        _ kind: AnalysisKind, media: MediaSnapshot, url: URL, urls: [UInt32: URL], cacheDir: URL
161	    ) -> Entry {
162	        let markerURL = AnalysisStore.markerURL(kind, media: media.id, in: cacheDir)
163	        let key = Key(
164	            media: media, url: url, lut: media.color?.lut.flatMap { urls[$0] },
165	            marker: Self.signature(of: markerURL))
166	        if let entry = memo[kind], entry.key == key { return entry }
167	        var entry = Entry(key: key, covered: [], boxes: [])
168	        if key.marker != nil,
169	            let marker = AnalysisStore.readMarker(kind, media: media.id, in: cacheDir),
170	            case let (input, fullRange) = ProjectDocument.analysisInput(
171	                media: media, url: url, urls: urls),
172	            let stamp = AnalysisStamp.make(
173	                kind: kind, media: media, url: url, input: input, fullRange: fullRange),
174	            marker.answers(for: stamp),
175	            let boxes = Self.boxes(kind, media: media.id, cacheDir: cacheDir)
176	        {
177	            entry = Entry(key: key, covered: AnalysisStore.merged(marker.ranges), boxes: boxes)
178	        }
179	        memo[kind] = entry
180	        return entry
181	    }

183	    /// Each sample's boxes and styles; nil when the payload does not decode.
184	    private static func boxes(_ kind: AnalysisKind, media: UInt32, cacheDir: URL)
185	        -> [[(rect: CGRect, style: Style)]]?
186	    {
187	        func rect(_ x: Float, _ y: Float, _ w: Float, _ h: Float) -> CGRect {
188	            CGRect(x: CGFloat(x), y: CGFloat(y), width: CGFloat(w), height: CGFloat(h))
189	        }
190	        switch kind {
191	        case .faces:
192	            guard let data = AnalysisStore.readPayload(
193	                .faces, media: media, file: AnalysisFaces.payloadName, in: cacheDir),
194	                let decoded = AnalysisFaces.decode(data)
195	            else { return nil }
196	            return decoded.samples.map { sample in
197	                sample.faces.map { (rect($0.x, $0.y, $0.width, $0.height), Style.face) }
198	            }
199	        case .subjects:
200	            guard let data = AnalysisStore.readPayload(
201	                .subjects, media: media, file: AnalysisSubjects.payloadName, in: cacheDir),
202	                let decoded = AnalysisSubjects.decode(data)
203	            else { return nil }
204	            return decoded.samples.map { sample in
205	                sample.subjects.salient.map {
206	                    (rect($0.x, $0.y, $0.width, $0.height), Style.salient)
207	                } + sample.subjects.people.map {
208	                    (rect($0.x, $0.y, $0.width, $0.height), Style.person)
209	                }
210	            }
211	        case .shots, .masks, .soundEvents, .foreground:
212	            return nil
213	        }
214	    }

216	    private static func signature(of url: URL) -> Signature? {
217	        var info = stat()
218	        guard stat(url.path, &info) == 0 else { return nil }
219	        return Signature(
220	            inode: UInt64(info.st_ino), size: Int64(info.st_size),
221	            seconds: Int(info.st_mtimespec.tv_sec), nanoseconds: Int(info.st_mtimespec.tv_nsec))
222	    }

225	
226	    /// The forward media's source tick under `playhead` in `clip`: through
227	    /// its source map when it ramps, its speed when not, mirrored about the
228	    /// media's duration when it plays backwards (`TimelineView.sourceTime`).
229	    static func sourceTick(
230	        of clip: ClipSnapshot, in media: MediaSnapshot, at playhead: Ticks, map: SourceMap?
231	    ) -> Ticks {
232	        TimelineView.sourceTime(of: clip, in: media, at: playhead, map: map)
233	    }

235	    /// The sample whose instant is the last at or before `source`:
236	    /// ⌊source · rate⌋, clamped to 0…lastIndex.
237	    static func sampleIndex(at source: Ticks, grid: AnalysisGrid) -> Int {
238	        min(grid.lastIndex, max(0, Int((Double(source) * grid.rate).rounded(.down))))
239	    }

241	    /// A normalised box (0…1, top-left, of the upright picture) placed in the
242	    /// layer's UNCROPPED rectangle and turned with the layer: its four
243	    /// corners in canvas pixels, TL TR BR BL.
244	    static func corners(of box: CGRect, on layer: CanvasLayerBox) -> [CGPoint] {
245	        let r = layer.uncroppedRect
246	        let placed = CGRect(
247	            x: r.minX + box.minX * r.width, y: r.minY + box.minY * r.height,
248	            width: box.width * r.width, height: box.height * r.height)
249	        return layer.corners(of: placed)
250	    }
